summary: Round 2 verification complete (stamp 065a928a776a1346). All 4 Round-1 findings are fixed and visually verified on fresh screenshots (wide-step-1-light.png, wide-step-6-light.png, tight-step-1-light.png, wide-step-6-dark.png) and updated source/audit files. Title block has clean spacing before 'm / rpm' in both wide and tight variants; both 5-spoke wheels and carrier flanges render cleanly with zero bow-tie cutout artifacts; the Step 6 slipping left tire now retains full 3D shading with a subtle slip tint in both light and dark modes; and Step 6 caption and narration clearly state the stall condition (192 N·m total is below the 410 N·m resistance holding the car still). findings.response: Fixed and verified visually on fresh screenshots (wide-step-1-light.png, tight-step-1-light.png, wide-step-6-light.png, wide-step-6-dark.png). findings.where: Step 6 slipping tire styling (wide-step-6-light.png; build.mjs CSS .rig-part[data-slip])
findings.finding: In Step 6 (wide-step-6-light.png), the slipping left wheel's tire loses all 3D shading and renders as flat pitch-black instead of tinted graphite. Because --rig-graphite-lit and --rig-graphite-dark reference themselves on the same element, CSS treats them as a custom-property cycle (guaranteed-invalid), causing the SVG faces to fall back to solid black. Mix against explicit base graphite color tokens (or hex values) rather than self-referencing the overridden properties.
findings.response: Fixed and verified visually in both wide-step-6-light.png and wide-step-6-dark.png. Replacing the self-referential variables with explicit base graphite hex values in .rig-part[data-slip] restores crisp 3D shading with a subtle slip tint in both light and dark modes.

findings.text: Because the open differential enforces equal torque, the dry wheel is capped at 96 N·m too — delivering only 192 N·m total and stranding 924 N·m of available grip. The dry right wheel stalls at 0 rpm while the icy left wheel spins at twice carrier speed, 440 rpm, spinning the spider gears at 352 rpm.
findings.finding: The caption states that 192 N·m total is delivered and immediately concludes that the dry right wheel stalls at 0 rpm without stating the physical condition for stalling: that 192 N·m is less than the resistance needed to get the car moving (e.g., starting on a slope, in snow, or against the 410 N·m load modelled here; on dead-flat dry asphalt, 192 N·m / 0.32 m = 600 N would exceed typical ~150–225 N rolling resistance). Briefly noting that 192 N·m is not enough to overcome the resistance holding the car still makes the 0 rpm stall physically complete.
findings.response: Fixed and verified in story.mjs and differential.audit.json (stamp 065a928a776a1346). Both the Step 6 caption and spoken narration now explicitly explain that 192 N·m total is less than the resistance holding the car still (410 N·m demand), making the 0 rpm dry-wheel stall physically airtight.
